method: Deterministic geometry on strictly parsed numbers, in inches, centimetres or millimetres converted to millimetres at exact factors (1 in = 25.4 mm, 1 cm = 10 mm). The belt is measured flat from the fold at the buckle: the centre hole sits the waist plus the fit allowance from the fold, the hole span is the spacing multiplied by one less than the hole count, and the first and last holes sit half that span either side of the centre. The finished belt adds the tip allowance beyond the last hole, and the strap blank adds the fold-back that wraps the buckle bar. Every hole position is listed with the waist that hole fits, which also answers the reverse question for an existing strap. Hole counts are odd and between 3 and 11 so one hole is the centre; a layout whose first hole would fall before the fold is refused, and one that leaves under 1 in (25.4 mm) of strap for the buckle is refused with a specific message instead of being clamped. The fit allowance is the crafter's own judgement of trousers, buckle thickness and preferred looseness. The tool does not model leather stretch, strap thickness, the length of the buckle itself or the shape of the tip, and it is a cutting plan rather than a fitting guarantee. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
